newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish bonds yields close higher, crown weakens.
newsitem.headline: Swedish bonds yields close higher, crown weakens.

text.p: Swedish debt yields rose on Thursday in part due to the European Commission's proposed stability pact for EMU members, dealers said.
The nine year bond yield closed up seven basis points at 7.33 percent after trading at 7.38 percent. Six month T-bill rates rose four basis points to 4.58 percent.
"One wonders if the rules in the pact are so hard that some countries such as Italy and Spain really will want to join the monetary union," one dealer said.
Other analysts said the explanation behind the weak debt market was much simpler.
"This is typical profit-taking. There is no fundamental reason for rising yields," an investor said.
The crown weakened to 4.3140 against the mark compared to 4.3050 late on Wednesday.
Market sources told Reuters the Riksbank defended the crown at 4.32 against the mark.
"The recent intervention by the Riksbank has created a trading range from 4.29 to 4.32," an analyst said.
No important events for the market were excepted on Friday.
